title: Rebuilding soil organic carbon at scale
bottleneck: Decades of intensive tillage have depleted soil organic carbon across the world's croplands, and rebuilding it is slow — carbon accrues over decades while farmers need returns in seasons. Measurement is expensive and uncertain, which stalls carbon markets that might pay for rebuilding; additionality and permanence disputes plague every soil-carbon credit scheme. The biology is also saturating: soils approach carbon equilibrium, limiting total gains. Measurement is expensive and uncertain, which stalls the carbon markets that might pay farmers for rebuilding.
why_it_blocks: Soil carbon underpins water retention, nutrient cycling, and yield resilience. Without rebuilding it, degraded soils can't sustain intensification.
current_state: Regenerative practices show carbon gains in trials; scaled, verified, paid-for soil carbon remains elusive. Soils also approach carbon equilibrium, limiting total gains no matter the practice.
